item.title: Bill Cosby ordered to pay $19.25m to woman in decades-old assault case | Africanews
item.description: A California court has awarded $19.25m in damages to a woman who accused actor Bill Cosby of drugging and sexually assaulting her somewhere in the early 1970s.

item.title: IMF plans Mozambique visit as debt pressures deepen | Africanews
item.description: Mozambique is set to host an International Monetary Fund mission in the coming months, as authorities seek support to manage growing financial pressures.

item.title: DR Congo plans to conduct second national census after 40 years | Africanews
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing to hold the second general census in its history, more than 40 years after the previous one, conducted in 1984.

item.title: Senegal fishermen bear the cost of industrial and illegal fishing | Africanews
item.description: In the port town of Rufisque, fishermen who have worked in these waters for decades say industrial and illegal fleets have stripped the sea bare. With no catch and no income, young men are now making a desperate choice: to leave.

item.description: Ghana’s embassy in the United States has criticised Lincoln University

item.title: Burundi arsenal blasts in Bujumbura kill 13 civilians | Africanews
item.description: Burundi’s army has confirmed that 13 civilians were killed and 57 others wounded after explosions tore through a military arsenal in Bujumbura earlier this week. Three soldiers were also reported among the injured, though no military deaths have been disclosed.

item.title: Nigeria: Bola Tinubu expected in Jos after deadly gun attack and mob violence | Africanews
item.description: Mob violence erupted on Wednesday in Jos, in north-central Nigeria, after a gun attack on a bar killed over 30 people during the weekend.

item.title: Pope calls for unity during Holy Thursday mass amid global tensions | Africanews
item.description: Pope Leo XIV led the Holy Thursday Chrism Mass at St. Peter’s Basilica, using the occasion to speak against the abuse of power and the drive for domination.

item.title: Uganda: Four children killed in knife attack at Kampala kindergarten | Africanews
item.description: The male suspect gained access to the daycare facility by posing as a parent, according to local media. Police said the four children killed were aged bewteen two and three.

item.title: Fally Ipupa marks 20 Years of solo career with historic Stade de France show [Interview] | Africanews
item.description: Fally Ipupa is celebrating 20 years of his solo career. For the occasion, he is releasing his eighth studio album, “XX", and inviting all music lovers to a major two-day celebration at the Stade de France on May 2 and 3.

item.title: From the Chrism Mass to the washing of the feet: Pope Leo’s first Easter season begins | Africanews
item.description: Pope Leo XIV begins his first Easter as pontiff by washing priests’ feet, following a tradition previously used by Pope Francis, while warning against domination in a troubled world.

item.title: Videos show explosions in central Iran as conflict with Israel intensifies | Africanews
item.description: Iran was hit by a powerful new wave of strikes on Wednesday when massive explosions and thick plumes of smoke rose over Baharestan, in the Esfahan region of central Iran.

item.title: Wall Street falls, oil surges after Trump threatens more attacks on Iran | Africanews
item.description: Stocks slumped and oil prices soared Thursday after President Donald Trump vowed the U.S. will continue to attack Iran and failed to offer a clear timetable for ending the conflict in the Middle East.
